messages:
jamal: deploy-bot just kicked an autorevert on the release (v3.6.1) — p95 latency breach during canary :warning:
deploy-bot: AUTOREVERT triggered for release v3.6.1 at 2025-10-02T15:17:56Z. Reason: latency_p95_usw2 > 600ms for 3 consecutive windows. Rolling back to v3.6.0.
jamal: logs look noisy, but curious if this is true regression or metrics spike from a noisy exporter.
erin: I see a large tail from the embed route around 15:16-15:18. Could be webhook flood from partner test.
Nina: @sre-ops can you confirm whether any infra events or scaling actions happened in usw2 at 15:10-15:20?
sre-ops: checking... nothing in infra events, but autoscaler logged a few upscales for gpu-pool-3 at 15:12. Attaching small snippet: ```
2025-10-02T15:12:03Z scaler INFO scale_up request_id=abc123 nodes=2->4 reason=queue_length
2025-10-02T15:13:12Z runtime WARN high_gc host=gpu-12 p95_latency=420ms
```
jamal: hmm autoscaler upscales usually reduce latency, not spike it. Could be KV cache coldstart combined with quantized kernel warmup.
erin: Agreed. We should not let deploy-bot yank the release if it's a transient warmup. What do others think — manual hold or let revert proceed? :thinking_face:
Nina: My take: pause the rollback and pin traffic slice to v3.6.0 for the affected tenant cohort, then run a quick synthetic with `canary-eval --promptset=latency-smoke` to repro. If repro, revert stays. If not, we can roll forward after a hotfix.
jamal: propose this plan: 1) manual override to stop further automated rollbacks 2) pin canary traffic to v3.6.0 for 20m 3) run synthetics and check KV cache hit rates + kernel logs 4) if no repro -> rollforward with hotpatch that increases kvcache prefill and disables one experimental kernel flag.
erin: +1. Who can flip manual override? @deploy-bot ops flag is `deploybot override hold <release>`
sre-ops: I can flip it now. Executing: `deploybot override hold v3.6.1 --by=sre-ops --reason="noisy metrics investigation"`
oncall-bot: Action recorded: deploybot override hold v3.6.1 by sre-ops at 2025-10-02T15:18:40Z
jamal: awesome. Nina can you run the canary-eval? I will prepare release note blurb in case we need to communicate a rollback or hotfix.
Nina: Running now. `canary-eval` output (truncated): ```
attempt 1: p95=620ms
attempt 2: p95=310ms
attempt 3: p95=290ms
kvcache_hit_rate: 0.12 -> 0.78 after prefill
```
jamal: interesting — first attempt spikes then stabilizes. That aligns with warmup hypothesis.
erin: decision: keep hold, mark as manual rollback suppressed, update release notes draft to explain ephemeral latency spike and planned hotpatch. Also set a 30m timer to unhold if metrics are stable.
jamal: I'll post the customer-facing note in #customer-communications after we confirm the hotpatch plan. Action items: sre-ops keep hold flag, nina complete 3 more synthetics, erin prepare hotpatch PR (disable kernel-flag `fastpath_v2`), jamal prepare note.
sre-ops: hold retained. Reopen window scheduled at 15:48 UTC unless an objection posted.
Nina: will post full eval results in 10m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
jamal: thanks all — pivot to comms if we need to announce rollback. For now this is a suppressed autorevert due to transient warmup; we won't notify customers unless the revert actually executes or the hotpatch affects behavior.
erin: noting in release tracker: `v3.6.1 - suppressed-autorevert - root_cause: kernel warmup + kvcoldstart (investigating)`
Nina: update: 3 more runs done, p95s: 300, 310, 295ms. Looks stable.
jamal: ok, schedule rollforward after hotpatch PR merges and 2 successful synthetics. I'll ping here when merging. :rocket:
